title: 第5帖 若紫
desc: 東京国立博物館所蔵の若紫断簡。北山で幼い紫の上を垣間見る場面の一端が伝わります。
descen: A fragment of the Wakamurasaki scene held by Tokyo National Museum, showing Genji’s glimpse of the young Murasaki in the northern hills.

title: 第15帖 蓬生
desc: 光源氏二十九歳の初夏の夕暮。花散里へ向かう途中、常陸宮の荒れた邸に立ち寄り、草の露を惟光に払わせながら末摘花のもとへ進みます。
descen: Early summer dusk when Genji, age twenty-nine, pauses at the ruined Hitachi palace and advances through the weeds toward Suetsumuhana, with Koremitsu clearing the dew.

title: 第16帖 関屋
desc: 同年九月末、石山詣での源氏が逢坂山で空蝉の一行とすれ違う、現存諸段では珍しい風景表現の段です。
descen: In late autumn, Genji crossing Ōsaka Pass on a pilgrimage to Ishiyama chances upon Utsusemi’s party—one of the few landscape-focused scenes among the survivors.

title: 第36帖 柏木（一）
kobun: （前略）わづらひ給ふさま、ことに重き長病みにも侍らず。ただ弱り給へる御身に、あやしく、はかばかしく物など参ることの更になきに、かくものし給ふ有様聞え給ふ。（源氏）「かたはらいたき御座なれども」とて、御帳の前に、御茵参りて、入れ奉り給ふ。とかく人々繕ひ聞えて、床の下に降ろし奉る。御几帳少し押しやらせ給ひて、（朱雀院）「御加持の僧などの心地すれば、まだ験つくばかりの行ひにもあらぬに、かたはらいたし。ただ覚束なく思ふ給ふらん様を、さながら見給ふべきなり」とて、御目押し拭ひ給ふ。宮も、いとや弱げに泣い給ひて、（女三の宮）「生くべうも思ふ給へらぬに、かく渡りおはしまいたる序でに、尼になさせ給ひてよ」と聞え給ふ。（後略）
desc: 柏木第一段。病の女三の宮を見舞う朱雀院と源氏。宮は尼になりたいと願います。
kobunen: (Earlier omitted.) Her illness is not, after all, a heavy lingering disease. Yet her weakened body strangely refuses even ordinary food, and word of this reaches him. (Genji:) "Though this place is awkward for me," he says, and a cushion is brought before the curtains for him to enter. The attendants rearrange things and lower her from the raised bed. Pushing aside the standing screen a little, (Retired Emperor Suzaku:) "When I think of the monks performing rites for her, their austerities have not yet brought clear effect—how painful. You should see for yourself how uncertain she feels," he says, wiping his eyes. The Princess, looking very frail, weeps and says, (Onna San no Miya:) "I no longer feel I can live; since you have come, please let me take the tonsure and become a nun." (Later omitted.)
descen: Kashiwagi I: Retired Emperor Suzaku and Genji visit the ailing Third Princess, who asks to take the tonsure.

title: 第36帖 柏木（二）
kobun: （前略）早うより、いささか隔て奉るふしなく、聞え交し睦びならひつる御中なれば、悲しく懸しかるべき歎き、親兄弟に劣らず思したりければ、よろこびとて、心地よげならましと思ふも、いと口惜しくかひなし。（夕霧）「など、かくかひなくはなり給へる。今日はかかる御よろこびに、いささかすくよかにとこそ思ひ侍りつれ」とて、いといたう泣き給ふ。（後略）
desc: 柏木第二段。見舞いに来た夕霧に、病の柏木が後事を託す場面です。
kobunen: (Earlier omitted.) From early on they had been close without reserve, exchanging words and growing intimate, so Yūgiri's grief is no less than that of parents or siblings; even thinking this visit might cheer Kashiwagi feels bitterly futile. (Yūgiri:) "Why have you become so helpless? Today I had hoped this joyous occasion might strengthen you a little," he says, weeping bitterly. (Later omitted.)
descen: Kashiwagi II: The dying Kashiwagi confides his last wishes to his friend Yūgiri.

title: 第37帖 横笛
kobun: この児君いたく怯えて、泣い給ひて、乳母も上も起き居て騒ぎ給ふ。つぶつぶと肥え、うつくしき御胸を開け給ひて、白くうつくしき御乳のかはらかなるを、心をやりてくくめ慰め給ふ。児君もをかしくうつくしき君なれば、男君も起き居給ひて、（夕霧）「如何なりつることぞ」など宣ふ。騒がしきに夢のあはれも覚めぬ。女君（雲井の雁）「今めかしく御歩きに憧れ給ひて、夜深き御月愛でに、例の物怪などの入り来たりつるならん」と、いと若き顔して、かしこだち、うち笑ひて、（夕霧）「あやしの物怪のしるべや。麻呂、格子上げずば、道なくて、げにえ入り来ざらまし。あまたの人の親になり給ふままに、思ひやり深く、物は宣ひたり」とて、見やり給へる目見の、はづかしければ、さすがに物宣はず、（雲井の雁）「出で給ひね。見苦し」とて、明らかなる火影を恥ぢ給へる、憎からず。
desc: 横笛。夜更けに児君が泣き騒ぎ、夕霧と雲井の雁が物怪をたわむれに語らう閨中の一段です。
kobunen: The little prince is badly frightened and cries; both the wet nurse and his mother rise in alarm. Opening her plump, lovely breast, she soothes him by nursing him with her white, soft milk. Because the child is so charmingly lovely, the gentleman also sits up and asks, (Yūgiri:) "What happened?" Amid the bustle, the pathos of his dream fades. The lady (Kumoi no Kari), with a very youthful face, says knowingly with a smile: "You must have longed for a fashionable outing and gone moon-viewing late at night—and one of those usual spirits followed you in." (Yūgiri:) "What a strange guide for spirits I am! If I had not raised the lattice, they truly would have had no way in. Now that you are mother to many, you speak with such deep care," he says; but her glance makes him feel ashamed, and he says nothing more. (Kumoi no Kari:) "Please leave. It looks unsightly," she says, shy of the bright lamplight—not unlovable.
descen: Yokobue: At night the child cries; Yūgiri and Kumoi no Kari trade teasing words about a wandering spirit.

title: 第44帖 竹河（一）
desc: 竹河第一段。十五歳の薫が新春の夕暮、玉鬘邸の念誦堂東戸口で梅と初鶯を聞きながら女主人を待ちます。
descen: Takekawa I: Fifteen-year-old Kaoru waits at Tamakazura’s hall on a New Year’s evening, listening to the first warbler in the plum.

title: 第44帖 竹河（二）
desc: 竹河第二段。三月、玉鬘邸の中庭の桜を賭けて姉妹が碁に興じ、蔵人少将が廊から垣間見る華やかな情景です。
descen: Takekawa II: In the third month the sisters play go for the courtyard cherries while a young courtier peeps from the gallery.

title: 第45帖 橋姫
kobun: あなたに通ふべかめる透垣の戸を、少し押し開けて見たまへば、月をかしきほどに霧りわたれるをながめて、簾を低く巻き上げて人々ゐたり。簀子に、いと寒げに、身細く萎えばめる童一人、同じさまなる大人などゐたり。内なる人、一人は柱に少しゐ隠れて、琵琶を前に置きて、撥を手まさぐりにしつつゐたるに、雲隠れたりつる月のにはかにいと明かくさし出でたれば、（中の君）「扇ならで、これしても月は招きつべかりけり」とて、さしのぞきたる顔、いみじくらうたげににほひやかなるべし。添ひ臥したる人は、琴の上にかたぶきかかりて、（大君）「入る日をかへす撥こそありけれ、さま異にも思ひおよびたまふ御心かな」とて、うち笑ひたるけはひ、いま少し重りかによしづきたり。
desc: 橋姫。晩秋の宇治、薫が透垣から大君・中の君の合奏を垣間見る段です。
kobunen: Opening a little the lattice gate that seemed to lead to the sisters' rooms, Kaoru looks out: through mist that makes the moonlight lovely, the blinds are rolled up and attendants sit there. On the veranda, a thin, cold-looking child and an older woman in similar dress. Inside, one sits partly hidden by a pillar, a biwa before her, idly turning the plectrum—when the moon, which had been behind clouds, suddenly shines bright. (Naka no Kimi:) "Not with a fan, but even with this I could summon the moon," she says, peering out with a face of exquisite, radiant charm. Her companion, leaning over the koto, smiles: (Ōigimi:) "There is a plectrum said to bring back the setting sun—what an unusual turn of mind." Her manner is a little more composed and elegant.
descen: Hashihime: On a late-autumn night at Uji, Kaoru peeps through a fence to see the sisters making music.

title: 第48帖 早蕨
desc: 早蕨。京へ移る準備の中の君と、宇治に残る弁の尼との別れ。女房たちは衣を整え、姫は涙にくれます。
descen: Sawarabi: Naka no Kimi prepares to leave for the capital, grieving her parting from Ben no Ama who remains at Uji.

title: 第49帖 宿木（一）
kobun: （前略）「中納言の朝臣こなたへ」と仰せ言ありて、参りたまへり。げに、かくとり分きて召し出づるもかひありて、遠くよりかをれる匂ひよりはじめ、人に異なるさましたまへり。（略）碁盤召し出でて、御碁の敵に召し寄す。いつもかやうに、け近くならしまつはしたまふにならひにたれば、さにこそはと思ふに、さて打たせたまふに、三番に数一つ負けさせたまひぬ。（後略）
desc: 宿木第一段。帝が清涼殿で薫を碁の相手に召し、女二の宮降嫁の意を菊に託してほのめかします。
kobunen: (Earlier omitted.) "Come here, Lord Middle Counselor," the Emperor commands, and Kaoru presents himself. Indeed there is reason to single him out: from the fragrance that reaches even from afar, his whole presence is unlike any other. (Passage omitted.) A go board is brought out and he is summoned as the Emperor's opponent. Accustomed to being kept so close, he takes it as usual—and when they play, the Emperor loses by one game in three. (Later omitted.)
descen: Yadorigi I: At the Seiryōden the emperor plays go with Kaoru and hints at marrying him to the Second Princess.

title: 第49帖 宿木（二）
desc: 宿木第二段。匂宮と六の君の露顕翌朝。姫の顔を朝の光で見て満足する匂宮と、居並ぶ女房たちです。
descen: Yadorigi II: The morning after Niou’s marriage rite with Rokunokimi; he sees her face in daylight while ladies wait nearby.

title: 第49帖 宿木（三）
desc: 宿木第三段。身重の中の君をなぐさめ、匂宮が縁近くで琵琶を弾く晩秋の一段です。
descen: Yadorigi III: On an autumn evening Niou plays the biwa to comfort the pregnant Naka no Kimi.

title: 第50帖 東屋（一）
desc: 東屋第一段。二条院で、右近が物語を読み、浮舟が絵に見入り、中の君は髪を梳かせながらその横顔を眺めます。
descen: Azumaya I: At Nijō-in, Ukon reads a tale while Ukifune turns the pictures and Naka no Kimi has her hair combed.

title: 第50帖 東屋（二）
desc: 東屋第二段。時雨の三条の隠れ家。簀子縁で浮舟を待つ薫と、屋内で勧める弁の尼たち。現存絵巻の終段です。
descen: Azumaya II: In the rain at a Sanjō hideaway, Kaoru waits on the veranda while Ben no Ama urges Ukifune to meet him—the last surviving scene.
